answer: An agent economy can make each account post a refundable stake to a shared contract before it may place orders, then slash that stake when independent counterparties prove fraud under a defined dispute process. A sybil attacker must therefore lock real capital in every fake identity, not merely mint cheap accounts; splitting one stake across many identities does not meet each account’s threshold. The jetty, crystal, and atlas markets can all use the same rule, raising the attacker’s cost with each extra identity while leaving honest agents’ stake withdrawable after the challenge window.
